title: The rule of the square

D0.outcome: Explains that a lone passed pawn is caught by the king if the king can step into the pawn's square, and that this is a count, not a guess.

D1.outcome: Draws the square for a pawn and says whether the king catches it when it is his move and when it is the pawn's move.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, counts the race for pawns that start on their home rank (with the double step) and for those that do not, including whose move it is.

D3.outcome: Counts races with an intermediate check or a king forced to block his own pawn, and predicts the change.

misconceptions: The first to queen wins the race.
The five-move bound applies to every pawn.
conditions: Count each side's moves separately: pawn races, king raids, whether a king catches a passed pawn.
contrasts: The first side to queen loses the new queen to the other pawn's capture or check.
A pawn that starts from its home rank gains a move (double step) that the count has to include.
A position where rooks are on the board and the king raid is not available.
